analogs.covers: Body and daily life: Australia's big tree-climbing monitor of wet forests (the profile's female subspecies is Varius). It climbs trunks to bask, hunt and get out of trouble, scavenges boldly, swims well and never lives far from water
The hunting pose: a motionless ambusher clinging to a trunk that lunges at the first flash of movement, bites hard and is famously irritable when disturbed

headline: A lace monitor that clings to the trunk like a tokay gecko: the tree dragon of the swamp forest that waits above the water and strikes at anything that moves.

setting.label: Swamp forests, bogs, riverbanks and waterfalls
setting.note: Twisted Forest with Roots Pond and Wollemi Forest for trees over water, Stillwater Bog, Mudflats and Coastland Swamp for wallowing and fishing, Lakeside Meadow and Grand Falls for group basking. Cliffedge Falls, Coastal Bluffs and East Passage at the edges. Courtship at the Hot Springs on the Volcano Islands.

playsLike: You live among the trunks and the water of Twisted Forest, Wollemi Forest and the bogs. Megalania can climb, and Dynasty made it climb faster, so you go up. You cling to a trunk above a game trail or a pond, still as a tokay gecko on a wall, tongue flicking, until something moves. Then you come down fast and strike, and if the prey runs, you run it down. You scavenge first, the way a lace monitor raids a picnic ground. The trunk is your lookout, your bed and your ambush point. The water is your way out, and you dive there for fish. You are the tolerant variant: two or three of you may share a sunny bank or a log over the river. You challenge any arid Megalania in your forest out.

why.text: Dynasty raised its climbing speed: "Climbing movement speed increased by 10%". A lace monitor spends much of its life on trunks, hunting, basking and escaping trouble there.

"A rustling bush or flash of motion can provoke them into immediate pursuit, racing in the direction of the movement." That is how a tokay gecko hunts from a wall: it ignores everything that stays still.
"They opt to ambush where possible, skulking in bushes, foliage and rocky areas to remain hidden." In a swamp forest, much of that foliage is up the trunk.

Like a lace monitor or Nile monitor that swims across rivers: "all Megalania enjoy swimming, and are capable of diving below the depths to catch fish or hunt small prey." It may use water freely in a fight.
Unlike the arid loners: "Two or three can be commonly spotted resting together by river banks, flicking their tongues lazily."
"Megalania who are disrupted from their rest may respond with aggression or a venomous bite". A tokay gecko is notorious for exactly that.

notLike: A tokay gecko fits in your hand and hunts at night. You are a cathemeral predator with 2,600 combat weight, so you take the gecko's pose and temper, not its size.
Climbing is for lurking, basking and watching, not for escaping a lost fight. Climbing out of reach on heavy deathscars is body denial (server rule 4.6).
Lace monitors are loners. Temperate Megalania share riverbanks with two or three others, which is the Nile monitor side of the official inspiration.
twist: The profile names the Nile monitor as this variant's inspiration. It is the river monitor that basks on branches over the water and drops in when disturbed, and that is your escape route too.
